references.text: The Lord predicts that He will harden Pharaoh's heart, so that he will not let the people go.
The Lord says that He will harden Pharaoh's heart and perform many signs and wonders in Egypt.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the Lord had said.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said.
Pharaoh hardened his own heart and did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he did not listen to them, just as the Lord had said.
Pharaoh's heart was hardened, and he would not let the Israelites go, just as the Lord had said through Moses.
The Lord says that He has hardened Pharaoh's heart and the hearts of his servants.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not let the Israelites go.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he was unwilling to let them go.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he would not let the Israelites leave his land.
The Lord says that He will harden Pharaoh's heart so that he pursues the Israelites.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he pursued the Israelites.
Paul quotes Scripture about Pharaoh and explains that God hardens whom He wills, using this as an example of God's sovereignty.
Explores the theological tension between God's hardening and Pharaoh's own will, both leading to disobedience.
Connects the prophecy about Pharaoh's hardened heart to its actual fulfillment in the action.
